title: Fluffy Tangzhong Japanese Milk Bread
summary: A small portion of flour is cooked with milk into a paste, then kneaded into an egg and butter enriched dough until silky. The dough is shaped into three rolls, proved together in a tin, brushed with milk and baked into a tall, feathery loaf.
equipment: 900 g (23 x 13 cm) loaf tin, buttered

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Tangzhong
steps.text: Cook the flour and milk to a thick paste at 65 °C and cool.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Knead with the dough ingredients, then work in the butter until silky.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll and fold 3 portions and prove them in the tin.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Brush with milk and bake until 88-90 °C in the centre.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Turn out and cool before tearing or slicing.

tips: The tangzhong traps water, which keeps the loaf soft for longer.
Knead until the dough stretches thin enough to see light through.
Pull the loaf apart in feathery strips or slice it thick for toast.
storage: Keep wrapped at room temperature for up to 3 days, or slice and freeze for up to 1 month and toast from frozen. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
